abstract:
In spatial omics, multi-omics data have the potential to delineate tissue architecture more faithfully than any single modality, but unsupervised spatial domain detection remains difficult because different modalities exhibit distinct sparsity patterns and noise characteristics. Existing methods have made progress in combining spatial and multimodal signals, yet how to introduce cross-modal information while preserving reliable modality-specific representations and avoiding non-local spot mixing remains insufficiently explored. To address this challenge, we present SPAMO, a cross-modal fusion framework for unsupervised spatial multi-omics domain detection.
SPAMO learns modality-specific graph representations by combining a spatial-based KNN graph shared across modalities with a modality-specific feature based KNN graph, performs neighborhood-constrained cross-modal attention over co-located and neighboring spots, and uses gated residual fusion to integrate unimodal and cross-modal information. Across Human Lymph Node, Mouse Brain, and simulated benchmarks, SPAMO achieves competitive or improved domain-detection performance, with the clearest gains on real datasets. These results support neighborhood-constrained cross-modal fusion as an effective strategy for retaining modality-specific representations while incorporating complementary multi-omics information.
Code is available on GitHub (https://github.com/ai4nucleome/SPAMO). The data and archived source code are available on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23411574).
Supplementary data are available online.
